subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In typography, what does the term 'typeface' refer to?
options: A single physical piece of metal type
A designed set of letters, numbers and symbols sharing a common style
The space between two individual letters
The horizontal line on which letters sit
questions.explain: A typeface is a family of characters unified by a consistent design style, such as Helvetica or Times New Roman.

questions.q: What is the key visual feature that distinguishes a serif typeface from a sans-serif typeface?
options: Small strokes or feet at the ends of the letters
The use of only capital letters
Letters joined together in a flowing script
A fixed width for every character
questions.explain: Serifs are the small finishing strokes at the ends of letterforms, absent in sans-serif ('without serif') typefaces.

questions.q: In typographic terms, what does 'kerning' adjust?
options: The spacing between individual pairs of letters
The vertical spacing between lines of text
The overall size of the type in points
The weight or boldness of a font
questions.explain: Kerning fine-tunes the horizontal space between specific letter pairs to improve visual balance.

questions.q: What does the term 'leading' describe in a text layout?
options: The vertical space between lines of type
The indentation of the first line of a paragraph
The most important headline on a page
The margin around the edge of the page
questions.explain: Leading is the vertical distance between the baselines of successive lines of text, affecting readability.

questions.q: Why do graphic designers often use an underlying grid when arranging a page layout?
options: To make the printing process cheaper
To organise elements consistently and create visual order and alignment
To ensure only one colour is used
To force all text to be centred
questions.explain: A grid provides an invisible structure that aligns text and images, giving the layout coherence and balance.

questions.q: A poster uses one very large, bold word at the top and smaller text below it. What layout principle is this mainly demonstrating?
options: Visual hierarchy
Kerning
Bleed
Registration
questions.explain: Varying size and weight establishes a visual hierarchy that guides the viewer's eye to the most important information first.

questions.q: Why might a designer choose a highly legible sans-serif typeface for road signage rather than a decorative script?
options: Because scripts cannot be printed in colour
Because clarity and quick legibility are essential for that purpose
Because sans-serif fonts are always cheaper
Because scripts cannot be enlarged
questions.explain: Signage must be read quickly and at distance, so a clear, legible typeface is more fit for purpose than a decorative one.

questions.q: What is the main effect of leaving generous 'white space' (empty space) in a layout?
options: It wastes paper and should be avoided
It can create a clean, uncluttered feel and draw attention to key elements
It always makes text harder to read
It reduces the number of colours needed
questions.explain: White space gives elements room to breathe, reducing clutter and helping focus the viewer's attention.

questions.q: You are designing a two-page magazine spread and want the columns of text on both pages to line up neatly. Which tool is most appropriate?
options: A colour wheel
A layout grid with consistent columns and margins
A single decorative typeface
A photographic filter
questions.explain: A shared grid ensures columns and margins align across both pages, giving the spread a professional, unified appearance.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a raster (bitmap) image and a vector image?
options: Raster images are made of pixels; vector images are made of mathematical paths
Raster images can only be black and white
Vector images always contain photographs
Vector images cannot be resized
questions.explain: Raster graphics store a grid of pixels, whereas vector graphics use mathematical points and lines that scale without loss of quality.

questions.q: Which type of image can be scaled up to a very large size without becoming blurred or pixelated?
options: A vector image
A low-resolution JPEG
A scanned photograph
A bitmap image
questions.explain: Because vectors are defined mathematically, they can be resized to any dimension while staying crisp.

questions.q: In digital colour work for screen-based media, which colour model is normally used?
options: RGB (red, green, blue)
CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, black)
Greyscale only
Pantone spot colours
questions.explain: Screens emit light and combine red, green and blue additively, so RGB is the standard model for on-screen work.

questions.q: Which colour model is normally used for full-colour commercial printing?
options: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, black)
RGB (red, green, blue)
HSB (hue, saturation, brightness)
Greyscale
questions.explain: Print uses subtractive inks, combining cyan, magenta, yellow and black (key) to reproduce full colour.

questions.q: A student wants to create a logo that will be used on both a business card and a large banner. Why is a vector illustration the better choice?
options: It uses fewer colours automatically
It can be resized to any scale without losing sharpness
It cannot be edited once made
It only works on screens
questions.explain: A vector logo stays crisp whether printed tiny on a card or enlarged onto a banner, unlike a fixed-resolution bitmap.

questions.q: Why might an illustrator combine hand-drawn marks with digital editing software in one image?
options: To avoid using any colour
To merge the character of handmade marks with the flexibility of digital editing
Because digital tools cannot produce colour
To make the file size as large as possible
questions.explain: Blending traditional and digital media lets an artist keep expressive hand-drawn qualities while gaining easy editing, layering and reproduction.

questions.q: What is one advantage of working with layers in digital illustration software?
options: Different elements can be edited separately without affecting the others
The image can only ever be saved in black and white
It prevents the image from being resized
It automatically removes all colour
questions.explain: Layers keep parts of an image independent, so an element can be moved or altered without disturbing the rest.

questions.q: You need to email a photograph for a small on-screen thumbnail and want a small file size. Which format and setting is most suitable?
options: A compressed JPEG at low resolution
An uncompressed high-resolution TIFF
A scalable vector file
A CMYK print-ready file
questions.explain: JPEG compression and a low resolution keep the file small, which suits a small on-screen thumbnail sent by email.

questions.q: In graphic communication, what is the main purpose of a logo?
options: To identify a brand or organisation with a memorable visual symbol
To provide a long written explanation of a product
To fill empty space on a page
To replace all photographs
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive mark that gives a brand or organisation an instantly recognisable visual identity.

questions.q: Why is it essential for a graphic designer to understand the target audience before designing?
options: So the style, imagery and message suit the people it is meant to reach
So the design can use every available colour
So the file will be smaller
So the printer runs faster
questions.explain: Knowing the audience lets the designer tailor visual language and tone so the message communicates effectively to that group.

questions.q: You are designing a poster to warn people of danger. Which choice would communicate the message most effectively?
options: Bold red colour, a clear warning symbol and large legible text
Pale pastel colours and a small decorative script
Only a photograph with no words
A dense block of small grey text
questions.explain: Strong colour, a recognised symbol and large clear type convey urgency and are read quickly, making the warning effective.
